# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-docs.mjs from plugins/landfall/lib/cli/commands.mjs; do not edit. Regenerate: node scripts/gen-docs.mjs -->

`landfall` is on the Bash tool PATH while the plugin is enabled. Agents call it with `--json` and read the envelope; people read the text output.

## Envelope

With `--json` every command prints exactly one line on stdout and nothing on stderr:

```json
{"cli":1,"command":"<name>","ok":<bool>,"code":<int>,"exit":"<NAME>","data":{…},"errors":[{"code":"<kebab>","message":"<≤ 300 chars>","hint":"<≤ 200 chars>"}]}
```

- `ok` is `true` exactly when `code` is 0; a non-zero code carries at least one error.
- Partial data: `ok: false` with `data` holding what was computed and `data.partial: true`.
- Without `--json`: text on stdout, errors with their hints on stderr.
- Output carries no escape sequence, control, bidi or invisible character from data: text drops them and keeps the printable rest; the envelope writes them as `\u` escapes, so `JSON.parse` gives the data back exactly.
- A command that changes files refuses without a terminal unless `--yes` is given: exit 7 REFUSED (REV-58). Consent is per form: a command section names each flag whose form differs.
- A command exits only with the codes its section lists, plus 2 USAGE (arguments) and 70 INTERNAL (bug); any other code is reported as 70.

## Exit codes

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | OK | success; for `tick`: do the listed steps now (ACTION) |
| 1 | FAIL | the command ran and the checked condition is false (verify failed, check found problems, claim held, merge conflict) |
| 2 | USAGE | unknown command or flag, invalid value, limit exceeded |
| 3 | WAIT | `tick`: work in progress; `wait`: run still running; `heavy`: no slot within --wait |
| 4 | DONE | `tick`: loop complete |
| 5 | STALLED | `tick`: no progress within the stall window; `heavy`: no output within --idle |
| 6 | BUDGET | `tick`: a cap was reached; `heavy`: the --timeout was reached |
| 7 | REFUSED | newer state schema, inactive repository for a write command, missing consent (no terminal and no `--yes`) |
| 8 | ENV | environment problem: not a git repository, git, claude or a provider CLI missing, network for lanes |
| 70 | INTERNAL | bug; the message asks for `doctor --json` output in an issue |

## Usage

```text
usage: landfall <command> [options]

Commands:
  baseline pin         Repair the test baseline: replace it with the inventory collected now, with a gate-change or test-removal decision.
  baseline show        Print the pinned test baseline: every test with its skip flag, pinned failures, collector and last pin.
  brief                Render the brief of a routed task from the brief template and the state; --write saves tasks/<id>/brief.md.
  commit               Commit the changes under the state directory as one chore commit; the code and the index outside it stay as they are.
  config set           Set one config value: a threshold override (only with an active decision) or the providers of an executor role.
  config show          Show the configuration: threshold overrides with their default and decision, executor preferences, changed flags.
  deactivate           Remove the untracked state of this repository (or the link of its external state) and remember the opt-out.
  decide               Record a decision: a new D-<H>-<n> file under the state directory with what, why and cost if wrong.
  decisions check      Validate the decision records and every D-<H>-<n> cited in tracked files; exit 1 on a problem.
  decisions find       List decisions matching all words; with --path, the ones cited in or scoped to that file.
  decisions retire     Retire a decision: status retired, the record kept, a tombstone so its ID is never used again.
  decisions show       Print one decision record.
  decisions supersede  Record a decision replacing an active one; the old record gets status superseded and supersededBy.
  decline              Opt out of tracking this repository; remembered in machine data by its real path, never in the repository.
  doctor               Health report: Claude Code floor, plugin and hooks, release, state, profile, flags, context cost, permissions.
  exec                 Start an external reviewer with a pinned review brief: latest round or --round; save with review brief <id> --write.
  findings add         File findings from a recorded review round, once per source task, round and finding ID.
  findings close       Mark open or taken backlog findings fixed by an existing task.
  findings drop        Drop open or taken backlog findings with a reason recorded in a decision.
  findings list        List review findings kept in the backlog; defaults to open and taken.
  findings show        Show a backlog finding, its source review and its lifecycle.
  findings take        Create one task for selected open backlog findings and mark them taken.
  flags set            Set one capability flag of this repository (off, shadow or on, as the flag has them); a flip is recorded as a decision.
  flags show           Show the capability flags: each rollout capability with its mode, its source and what it does, then the team flags.
  gen apply            Write the generated files (CI workflow, pre-push hook, PR template, CODEOWNERS and AGENTS.md blocks); edits survive.
  gen plan             Show what gen apply would do for each generated file; writes nothing.
  heavy                Run a heavy command (full tests, build) in the machine-wide FIFO queue under a heavy lease, with time and output limits.
  init                 Activate tracking in this repository: state.json, .gitignore and your handle in team/<H>.json.
  install              Install the plugin for an agent without it (npx channel): run the SD-3 commands with claude, or print them.
  lane claim           Claim a lane on origin for 7 days: free → yours, yours → renewed, another's past expiry + 24 h → taken over.
  lane list            List the lane claims on origin: lane, owner, expiry, and whether it is live, expired or open for takeover.
  lane release         Release your lane: its claim on origin is deleted only while it is still the one you hold (lease).
  lane renew           Renew your lane for 7 more days; at most once a day (a claim made less than 24 h ago is kept as it is).
  lane takeover        Take over another developer's lane once its claim expired more than 24 h ago; the new claim records it.
  loop start           Start a loop with caps (defaults: wallMin=480,ticks=200,usd=25,rounds=2); a running loop is never replaced.
  loop status          Print the loop: ticks, wall time and cost against the caps, the stall count, and the exit once it ended.
  loop stop            End the running loop: exit DONE, so no wakeup is scheduled again; an ended loop is left as it is.
  method               Print one pack or one section of the method by name, or the names of every pack and section.
  migrate              Run the forward migrations on every state file of this repository; --dry-run lists the steps and writes nothing.
  profile gates apply  Replace the profile gates with the candidates the scan detects; only with an active gate-change decision.
  profile gates set    Add a profile gate or replace the one of that name; only with an active gate-change decision.
  profile observe      Scan the repository (manifests, files, CI, harnesses) and merge what it shows into the project profile.
  profile set          Record one profile fact with its source and evidence: the user's words (said) or a path:line (observed).
  profile show         Print the project profile: facts with source and evidence, gates, risk paths, and whether a scan is due.
  providers            List the provider CLIs for external runs: found on PATH, version, auth, roles and the sandbox per role.
  providers add        Declare another provider CLI (generic adapter): its argv template and the sandbox mode per role.
  receipt              Tokens and cost of a task, a run, the loop, or all work since a day (default: since activation) by class or executor.
  report               Store a task report from a file (RED/GREEN checked); --round appends a fix round; records the implementer event.
  review brief         Review brief of a task: range pinned to HEAD, diff saved to a file, acceptance, risks, output shape; --write saves it.
  review record        Record a typed review result as the next round tasks/<id>/review-r<k>.json; the Markdown review closes nothing.
  route                Classify a task as trivial, standard or critical from its plan and print its route; the class only rises.
  rule                 Print method rules by ID; a retired ID prints its successor. --core prints the always-on rules.
  runs                 List the external runs: queued, running, finished (newest first).
  runs list            List the external runs (same as runs).
  runs prune           Delete finished run records (and logs) older than 30 days, at most 200 a call.
  runs show            Print one external run record, or with --summary the short summary.
  runs stop            Stop an external run: SIGTERM to its supervisor, only when the recorded pid and start time still match.
  secrets              Scan for secrets and key files: working tree and index, staged changes, a commit range or a built artifact.
  slots                Show the machine scheduler: calibration, load and free memory, leases with ports and DB names, FIFO queues.
  slots calibrate      Calibrate the scheduler: cores, RAM, memory method; save LOAD_MAX, FREE_MIN and per-kind max overrides.
  state unlock         Remove a lock left by a process that is gone (store and machine data); writes never take one over.
  status               Show this repository: activation, tier, open tasks with their next step, the loop and leases; the default command.
  task done            Mark your task done; only after a passing verify for the code at HEAD (the only way to status done).
  task list            List the tasks of this repository: ID, status, class, round, kind, lane, branch, title.
  task merge           Merge a task branch with --no-ff --no-commit, run the outcome gates on the merged tree, commit only on pass.
  task new             Create a task with the next ID of your handle (T-<H>-<n>); area gates and releases are --kind gate.
  task set             Record a state of your task as an event with author and time; it moves the task's status.
  task show            Print one task as its resume card: class, branch, base, worktree, verify, reviews, open findings, next step, events.
  task start           Create the task's worktree and branch from a base commit and record them (started); the brief carries both.
  tick                 One loop tick: the next steps from the task state; exit ACTION (0), WAIT (3), DONE (4), STALLED (5) or BUDGET (6).
  tier                 Evaluate the project tier (L0-L3) from git history and the state; a change is logged (shadow) or recorded (on).
  verify               Re-run the profile gates, compare the test inventory with the baseline and record verify.json for a task.
  wait                 Wait for an external run: exit 3 while it runs, exit 0 with a short summary once it ended.

Options:
  --json         print exactly one JSON envelope line on stdout
  --yes, -y      consent for a command that changes files when no terminal is attached
  --help, -h     show help; with a command: help for that command
  --version, -V  print the version

Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 3 WAIT · 4 DONE · 5 STALLED · 6 BUDGET · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV · 70 INTERNAL
Reference: docs/cli.md · landfall <command> --help
```

## Commands

### `landfall baseline pin [--decision <D>] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall baseline pin [--decision <D>] [--yes] [--json]

Repair the test baseline: replace it with the inventory collected now, with a gate-change or test-removal decision.
For a collector change or a resolved tests.json conflict. The test gates run as in verify; their failures are pinned
as pre-existing; the baseline records the decision (pinnedBy). Refused, nothing written: a gate that cannot run (8),
a timeout, focused tests, a failing gate whose failures are not all collected (1).
Verify compares with the baseline committed at the task base (task merge: at the target tip), so pin on the target
branch and commit it; a task based before the pin takes that commit as its base.

Options:
  --decision <D>  required: an active gate-change or test-removal decision, such as D-AB-3

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

```text
usage: landfall baseline show [--json]

Print the pinned test baseline: every test with its skip flag, pinned failures, collector and last pin.
Exit 1 when its sha256 does not match its content (it was edited outside verify and baseline pin). Writes nothing.

Read-only.
```

### `landfall brief <id> [--role <role>] [--write] [--force] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall brief <id> [--role <role>] [--write] [--force] [--yes] [--json]

Render the brief of a routed task from the brief template and the state; --write saves tasks/<id>/brief.md.
Filled from the state: title and ID, the agent of the role, the class with the reason of its route record and the
kind, branch and base once recorded, the rule IDs of the role and the class, the profile gates, and the lease env
of a live lease the scheduler holds for the task here. Every other <…> placeholder is left to fill in.
The brief ends with a marker line holding its hash: --write replaces a saved brief while nobody edited it; one
written or edited by hand only with --force (else exit 1). Exit 1 also: no such task, the task is not routed.

Arguments:
  id  task ID such as T-AB-1

Options:
  --role <role>  implementer (default) or reviewer: the agent and the rules of the role
  --write        save it as tasks/<id>/brief.md in the state directory (the task's owner)
  --force        with --write: replace a brief written or edited by hand

Read-only. Changes files with --write: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall commit [--message <text>] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall commit [--message <text>] [--yes] [--json]

Commit the changes under the state directory as one chore commit; the code and the index outside it stay as they are.
Stages and commits only paths under the state directory (git add -A and git commit with that pathspec), with the message
"chore(<bin>): <what changed>" (the task IDs, decision IDs and files touched) unless --message says otherwise. The commit runs
your hooks (a refusing hook: exit 1, the paths stay staged). Nothing changed: exit 0. A state directory outside the repository
(init --state-dir) has nothing git tracks: exit 0, nothing done. The state is not code: verify and task done ignore it, so one
commit after a task is enough.

Options:
  --message <text>  the commit message (one line of at most 200 characters; default: chore(<bin>): <what changed>)

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall config set <key> <value> [--decision <D>] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall config set <key> <value> [--decision <D>] [--yes] [--json]

Set one config value: a threshold override (only with an active decision) or the providers of an executor role.
Keys: thresholds.<unit>.<path> (a whole number of lib/router or lib/engine thresholds.json, such as
thresholds.router.trivial.maxLoc) and executors.reviewer|implementer (providers in order, comma-separated).
A threshold override needs --decision with an active decision (else exit 1, nothing written); config.json keeps
the decision with the value. The value default removes an override or a preference. Flags: use flags set.
Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes.

Arguments:
  key    thresholds.<unit>.<path> or executors.<role>
  value  a whole number, a comma-separated provider list, or default

Options:
  --decision <D>  required for a threshold override: an active decision, such as D-AB-3

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall deactivate [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall deactivate [--yes] [--json]

Remove the untracked state of this repository (or the link of its external state) and remember the opt-out.
State tracked by git is never removed: exit 1 with the git rm command to run first, nothing changed.
An external state directory keeps its files; only its link is removed. Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes.

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall decide [--title <text>] [--why <text>] [--cost <text>] [--scope <globs>] [--kind <kind>] [--supersedes <ids>] [--allows-test-removal <ids>] [--from-verify <task>] [--from-file <json>] [--task <id>] [--remaining <ids>] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall decide [--title <text>] [--why <text>] [--cost <text>] [--scope <globs>] [--kind <kind>] [--supersedes <ids>] [--allows-test-removal <ids>] [--from-verify <task>] [--from-file <json>] [--task <id>] [--remaining <ids>] [--yes] [--json]

Record a decision: a new D-<H>-<n> file under the state directory with what, why and cost if wrong.
The number is the next of your handle: above every local record and tombstone and every one on origin/main.
--supersedes marks each listed active decision superseded by the new one (the only edit of another record).
--allows-test-removal lists test IDs in allowsTestRemoval; a JSON ID such as ["file","title",1] keeps its commas.
--task with --remaining (review-close): once the latest review round reaches the loop's rounds cap (default 2) and
remaining lists every blocking finding ID of that round, the review step counts as approved; gates and report do not.
--from-verify <task> takes the tests the task's latest verify saw removed or newly skipped as allowsTestRemoval (title,
kind test-removal and scope filled in unless given). --from-file <json> reads the fields from a JSON object (title, why,
cost, scope, kind, supersedes, allowsTestRemoval, task, remaining); a flag given here wins over the file.
Cite it next to the code it constrains (COD-12): "// D-<H>-<n>: <why in five words>".

Options:
  --title <text>               what was decided, one line (required, ≤ 120 chars)
  --why <text>                 why (required); its first sentence is shown when a file citing it is edited
  --cost <text>                cost if the decision is wrong (required); its first clause is shown too
  --scope <globs>              comma-separated path globs it constrains (≤ 20, ≤ 120 chars; ** * ? {a,b})
  --kind <kind>                general (default), tier, tier-pin, route-override, test-removal, gate-change, takeover or review-close
  --supersedes <ids>           comma-separated IDs of active decisions this one replaces
  --allows-test-removal <ids>  comma-separated test IDs verify may see removed or newly skipped (as verify prints them); kind test-removal by default
  --from-verify <task>         allow the tests the task's latest verify saw removed or newly skipped (a test-removal decision)
  --from-file <json>           read the fields from a JSON file (a regular file of at most 64 KB); flags given here win
  --task <id>                  the task whose review step a review-close decision closes; kind review-close by default
  --remaining <ids>            comma-separated blocking and minor finding IDs left open in the latest review; files them in the backlog

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall decisions check [--ci] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall decisions check [--ci] [--json]

Validate the decision records and every D-<H>-<n> cited in tracked files; exit 1 on a problem.
Problems: a cited ID that is unknown, retired or superseded (superseded: with --ci or the CI variable set; a
warning otherwise), duplicate IDs, frontmatter errors, supersedes references and cycles. Citations are read
from tracked files outside the state directory. Without an active state directory there is nothing to check.

Options:
  --ci  strict: a cited superseded decision is an error (also when CI is set)

Read-only.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall doctor [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall doctor [--json]

Health report: Claude Code floor, plugin and hooks, release, state, profile, flags, context cost, permissions.
Runs `claude --version`, `claude plugin list --json`, `claude plugin details` and `claude plugin marketplace list --json`,
and `git ls-remote` on the marketplace source for the newest release tag (2 s cap; unknown when offline); writes nothing.

Read-only.

```

### `landfall exec [--task <id>] [--role <role>] [--provider <id>] [--round <k>] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall exec [--task <id>] [--role <role>] [--provider <id>] [--round <k>] [--yes] [--json]

Start an external reviewer with a pinned review brief: latest round or --round; save with review brief <id> --write.
The provider is selected like the dispatch does (found, logged in, declared for the role; --provider names one). The
record starts as {status: starting}; the supervisor (run-supervise) takes the external lease (queued while none is
free), runs the provider in its own process group under the wall cap (reviewer 900 s, implementer 2700 s, or the env
<PREFIX>EXTERNAL_TIMEOUT), feeds the saved brief on stdin and keeps the record current at most once a second:
running, elapsedMs, tokens, lastLine; at the end exit, outFile, tokens and the status done, failed or timeout. On the
cap the whole group gets SIGTERM, a grace, then SIGKILL; the lease is released only after the group is gone.
A reviewer runs read-only in the repository checkout; the out file lives in a private temp directory (0700). Exit 1:
no such task, no saved brief (brief <id> --write), a live run of the task and role. Implementer runs: not yet (exit 2).

Options:
  --task <id>      required: the task ID, such as T-AB-1
  --role <role>    required: reviewer or implementer
  --provider <id>  a declared or built-in provider instead of the selection
  --round <k>      review brief round, 1 to 999 (default: highest stored round)

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall findings take [<ids…>] [--all] [--title <text>] [--yes] [--json]`


### `landfall heavy <cmd…> [--e2e] [--timeout <s>] [--idle <s>] [--wait <s>] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall heavy <cmd…> [--e2e] [--timeout <s>] [--idle <s>] [--wait <s>] [--json]

Run a heavy command (full tests, build) in the machine-wide FIFO queue under a heavy lease, with time and output limits.
Usage: heavy [options] -- <cmd…>. One queue entry per worktree; it starts only while load and free memory pass the
calibration (it waits in its queue place meanwhile). With more than one slot, the first (max − in use) tickets may take
a free slot in any order among them; no ticket behind them overtakes. The command runs at low priority with the lease env
(port block, test-DB name) and thread limits; the lease is released when it ends, before results are looked at.
The command leads its own process group: a limit, Ctrl-C or SIGTERM ends the whole group. Its output is shown when it
ends: the last 64 KB (data.output with --json). Exit 1: the command failed (its status in data) or the worktree already has a queue entry.
<PREFIX> is the env prefix of the plugin, as in the lease variables <PREFIX>PORT_BASE, PORT_MAX, DB_NAME and SLOT.

Arguments:
  cmd  the command and its arguments, after --

Options:
  --e2e          take the exclusive e2e lease instead of heavy
  --timeout <s>  hard wall-time limit in seconds (default 2700, or the env <PREFIX>HEAVY_TIMEOUT): exit 6
  --idle <s>     no-output limit in seconds (default 600): exit 5
  --wait <s>     longest wait for a slot in seconds (default 3600; 0: one try): exit 3

Read-only.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 3 WAIT · 5 STALLED · 6 BUDGET · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall lane claim <lane> [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall lane claim <lane> [--yes] [--json]

Claim a lane on origin for 7 days: free → yours, yours → renewed, another's past expiry + 24 h → taken over.
A claim is a branch ref per lane on origin holding an empty commit whose message is {lane, handle, at, expires}.
Every write is a compare-and-swap on origin (push --force-with-lease with the claim seen), so of two racing
developers one wins. Exit 1 while another developer holds the lane: its owner, expiry and the time takeover opens.
A network error exits 8 and never counts as a free lane; offline in a solo project: exit 0, nothing done.

Arguments:
  lane  lane: [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,39}, a valid git ref name
```

```text
Classify a task as trivial, standard or critical from its plan and print its route; the class only rises.
Critical: a path matching a risk glob, a risk flag, or a large change; trivial: a small change without flags.
Thresholds and default risk globs are data (lib/router/thresholds.json); --json lists every reason for the class.

An override waives only the reasons recorded before it; any other reason raises the class again.

The outcome gates are the same for every class.
```

### `landfall secrets [--range <revs>] [--staged] [--artifact <path>] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall secrets [--range <revs>] [--staged] [--artifact <path>] [--json]

Scan for secrets and key files: working tree and index, staged changes, a commit range or a built artifact.
Default: tracked files and untracked files that are not ignored, and what the index holds. --staged: the lines added
in the index. --range: the lines every commit of the range adds (also a secret added and removed again) and the key
and env files it adds (a merge: what it adds against every parent). --artifact: every file under a built file or
directory, ignored or not. BOM-marked UTF-16 text is decoded in every mode; other binary files are skipped. A file over
16 MiB in a diff is not read: it is listed as "not scanned" (data.skipped) and changes no exit.
Patterns: lib/secrets/patterns.mjs and the project's secrets-patterns.txt in the state directory (UTF-8, one per line,
the syntax of guard-extra.txt). A line holding the word SYNTH or "check-secrets: synthetic" is a synthetic test value
(SEC-11); in an artifact nothing is exempt. Findings print path:line (commit:path:line in a range), the pattern and the first
characters and length of the match, never the value. Exit 8: the scan could not run (not a git repository, a git
error, an unreadable file or pattern file, a refused pattern): the result is invalid, never clean. Run it without a pipe.

Options:
  --range <revs>     revisions as git log takes them, such as A..B or "<sha> --not --remotes" (options: --not --all --branches --remotes --tags)
  --staged           only the lines added in the index
  --artifact <path>  a built file or directory, relative to the current directory

Read-only.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall slots [--unlock-stale] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall slots [--unlock-stale] [--yes] [--json]

Show the machine scheduler: calibration, load and free memory, leases with ports and DB names, FIFO queues.
Leases are machine-wide: agent (implementer subagents), external, e2e and heavy, each with a port block and a test-DB name.
A lease is stale when its holder process is gone (pid, start time and how it was read; never the pid alone), or an agent
lease missed its heartbeat for its TTL; a holder that cannot be identified holds it until its TTL and is never signalled.
The next acquire reaps a stale lease and ends the members left in the process group of its recorded command. This
listing writes nothing.
A scheduler call never removes a lock left by a crashed process (exit 7); --unlock-stale does, when its owner is gone
and it stayed unchanged for 2 seconds (changes files: needs a terminal or --yes).

Options:
  --unlock-stale  remove the scheduler lock of a process that is gone (after a crash, while no scheduler call runs)

Read-only. Changes files with --unlock-stale: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall task merge [<id…>] [--branch <branch>] [--ready] [--adopt] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall task merge [<id…>] [--branch <branch>] [--ready] [--adopt] [--yes] [--json]

Merge a task branch with --no-ff --no-commit, run the outcome gates on the merged tree, commit only on pass.
A conflict or a failing gate aborts the merge (exit 1) and leaves the branch as it was; the tree must be clean.
The outcome gates: profile gates, test baseline, report evidence, state files (no route or review). A merge is
recorded on the task (a merged event and mergedAt). --adopt records tasks merged by hand after one gate run on HEAD:
each task whose branch tip is an ancestor of HEAD; the others are reported. A failing gate records nothing.
Any change to the gates needs a new gate-change decision. The commit runs your hooks; a hook that changes the
tree undoes the commit (the merge stays staged).
Several IDs, or --ready (the done, unmerged tasks with a branch), merge as one batch: the branches merge with
--no-ff in a temporary worktree, the gates run once on the integrated tree, a failure is bisected and only the
passing tasks merge, a conflict leaves only that task out, the target is fast-forwarded only if it did not move,
and a branch that changes the gates is skipped (merge it alone). One line per task, the gate runs, the batch id.

Arguments:
  id  task ID such as T-AB-1 (several: one batch, or with --adopt)

Options:
  --branch <branch>  the branch or commit to merge (default: the task's branch)
  --ready            merge every done, unmerged task with a branch as one batch, in task order
  --adopt            record tasks already merged by hand into HEAD, after one gate run on HEAD

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

```text
· cancelled --reason <t> · fix-round --round <k> --addressed <n> --open <n> · self-verified [--round <k>] · status-request.

  --addressed <n>    fix-round: findings addressed
```

### `landfall tick [--plan <file>] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall tick [--plan <file>] [--json]

One loop tick: the next steps from the task state; exit ACTION (0), WAIT (3), DONE (4), STALLED (5) or BUDGET (6).
The wakeup prompt is fixed and carries no task state (printed with WAIT). ACTION: do the steps, tick again. WAIT: schedule
one wakeup after NEXT_TICK seconds. DONE, STALLED, BUDGET: the loop ended; schedule nothing, cancel a pending wakeup, report.
The first tick starts a loop with the default caps (8 h, 200 ticks, $25 estimated cost, 2 fix rounds per task). A cap
reached (wall time, ticks, cost since the start from the transcripts and run records) → BUDGET. A cost that is a lower
bound is partial (data.partial, the reasons as errors); 3 ticks in a row whose cost cannot be measured → BUDGET. The same
state (git heads, the files under tasks/, run statuses) for 3 ticks over ≥ 30 min with no live run → STALLED. Every task
done or cancelled and the state directory committed → DONE. The exit is written to local/loop.json before it is printed;
every later tick returns it. Writes only that loop record (never committed), so it needs no --yes. Exit 7 in an inactive
repository.

Options:
  --plan <file>  a plan whose "### Task <id>: <title>" entries the loop must finish (relative to the repository root); a docs/plans/*.md plan travels in the wakeup prompt

Read-only.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 3 WAIT · 4 DONE · 5 STALLED · 6 BUDGET · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall tier [--explain] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall tier [--explain] [--yes] [--json]

Evaluate the project tier (L0-L3) from git history and the state; a change is logged (shadow) or recorded (on).
Signals: loc, modules, contributors30, parallelTasks, incidents30 and the deployedToUsers fact; thresholds are data
(lib/engine/thresholds.json). A tier rises when an up threshold holds today and falls only after the dwell days all
under the down threshold; at most one change per 7 days. Mode: the engine flag (flags show), shadow by default:
shadow logs the change as a proposed decision in local/shadow.jsonl and enforces nothing; on writes a tier decision
record and sets the lanes, ci-gate, pre-push, codeowners and pr-template flags; off refuses (exit 7).
An inactive repository is evaluated and nothing is written. The outcome gates are the same at every tier.

Options:
  --explain  one line per signal: its value, thresholds and dwell, and the change cadence

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

### `landfall verify <id> [--ci] [--no-cache] [--yes] [--json]`

```text
usage: landfall verify <id> [--ci] [--no-cache] [--yes] [--json]

Re-run the profile gates, compare the test inventory with the baseline and record verify.json for a task.
The gates run here (sh -c, their time limits); the report's prose never changes the result.
A removed or newly skipped test fails unless an active decision lists it in allowsTestRemoval; only new failures fail.
The class is re-classified from the diff against the task base and only rises; the report needs red and green
evidence in its frontmatter, the route its approved review. On pass the baseline grows.
Results: pass (0) · fail, baseline-shrunk, route-escalated, missing-artifact (1) · error (8: a gate could not run).
Only the task's owner verifies with writes; changes files: needs a terminal or --yes (in CI: --ci --yes).
A gate set that passed on this exact tree (clean worktree, same gates and plugin version, within 24 h) is reused from
local/gate-cache in the state directory instead of running again; the output says "gates: reused from <time>".

Arguments:
  id  task ID such as T-AB-1

Options:
  --ci        check only: write nothing (verify.json, baseline, class); no registered owner needed
  --no-cache  run the gates even when a passing run of this tree is stored

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 2 USAGE · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

## Internal commands

Hidden from `--help`; generated files call them.

### `landfall hook <name>`

```text
usage: landfall hook <name>

Hook entry point named in hooks/hooks.json; reads the hook event JSON on stdin.
Hooks are listed in lib/hooks/registry.mjs. Malformed input or an unknown hook name: no output (allow).
A guard that cannot verify a Bash command holding a guarded token (an error, over its time budget, input over the size cap, a broken install) blocks it with exit 2 and the reason on stderr.

Arguments:
  name  hook name from the registry

Internal: called by generated files; an error ends with exit 0 and no output, except a guard that cannot verify a guarded command (exit 2).
Exit codes: 0 OK
```

```text
usage: landfall run-supervise <run> [--yes] [--json]

Supervise one external run (started by exec): lease, process group, wall cap, record updates.
Internal: exec starts it detached, one per run. It takes the external lease, runs the provider, updates the record and releases the lease after the group is gone.

Arguments:
  run  the run ID from exec

Changes files: needs a terminal or --yes, otherwise exit 7 REFUSED.
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 FAIL · 7 REFUSED · 8 ENV
```

